question: Can predicted probabilities be trusted?
data: UCI Bank Marketing: 45,211 records and 16 predictors; subscription is the positive class.
method: Five stratified holdouts; training-only preprocessing and cross-validated probability calibration.
formula: Brier = mean((p - y)^2); ECE = sum(bin share × |mean p - mean y|).
interpretation: Lower Brier and log loss indicate better probability predictions. ECE depends on the chosen bins; a constant prevalence forecast can have low ECE while having no discrimination. Split bootstrap intervals are descriptive because holdouts overlap.
status: RECORDED EXTERNAL-DATA STUDY | full experiment not rerun in this review
table_title: Selected recorded values (units and context shown)
evidence_note: Selected committed results; source values were not independently retrained in this review.
finding: Isotonic calibration reduces mean Brier score from 0.0720 to 0.0693 across five holdouts, while ROC-AUC stays near 0.906. This supports a probability-quality improvement under the frozen protocol, rather than a substantial change in ranking. The call-duration ablation matters operationally because duration is unavailable before a call; results using it describe a retrospective task.
